summary: Soft-boiled egg with shiso and kochujang: a room-temperature egg boiled 4 minutes (or to your preference) and served over toasted baguette slices with shiso chiffonade, Meyer lemon olive oil, diluted kochujang, fleur de sel and pepper; a single serving written while the author was sick.
glance: room temperature, boiled 4 minutes for a pretty runny yolk
kochujang diluted with a bit of water to a spoonable sauce
faq: How long do I boil the egg?

Cover the egg by an inch of water, bring to a boil, add the egg, find a simmer and boil for 4 minutes, or to your preference. The author likes his pretty runny. Use a room-temperature egg or sit it in warm water for a few minutes.
What is kochujang?
Korean hot sauce, also spelled gochujang. Dilute it with a bit of water to make a spoonable sauce.
What is shiso?
The beefsteak plant leaf, here cut in thin ribbons (chiffonade) for the plate.
What olive oil goes on the toast?
Meyer lemon olive oil; the author suggests O brand. There's lots on the toast and a few more drops on the plate.
Why this combination?
Written while the author had pneumonia and a fever: when you are under the weather, sometimes strange things sound good.

summary: Panko-crusted egg with cherry-smoked asparagus, smoked paprika and sherry gastrique: hard-boiled egg halves coated in cornstarch, beaten egg and panko and pan-fried until crispy, served with smoked asparagus and a reduced sherry vinegar and sugar gastrique; serves 4.
glance: 3 hard-boiled (only 2 needed, a spare in case one cracks) and 1 raw for battering
1 cup sherry vinegar and 1/2 cup sugar reduced until it lightly coats a spoon
24 fat spears, blanched 2 minutes and smoked about 10 minutes
faq: Is stovetop smoking safe?

The author's note says he no longer recommends jury-rigged stovetop smoking because creating smoke in a low-oxygen sealed environment creates unnecessarily high levels of carcinogens; he points to his Smoked Tofu Buns recipe for a safer alternative, or smoking on a barbecue with real charcoal and wood chips.
How do you make a panko-crusted egg?

Hard boil, chill and peel the eggs, cut in half lengthwise, then batter the outside the usual way: cornstarch, then raw beaten egg, then panko mixed with salt. Try not to get any batter on top of the egg. Pan-fry in about 1/2 inch of oil until crispy.
Why panko on an egg?
The author was hunting for new ways to add crispy textures in unexpected places; the crunchy panko is a cool counterpoint to a correctly cooked, soft and smooth hardboiled egg.
What is a gastrique?
Here a reduction of sherry vinegar and sugar (with a pinch of salt) that adds complex sweet, sour and caramelized notes. Cook it until it lightly coats a spoon after a minute of cooling.
How do I finish the asparagus?
Trim to 3-inch lengths, lightly peel the stems, blanch 2 minutes and shock in ice water, smoke (the author used cherry wood), then reheat with a quick high-heat saute in olive oil.

summary: Farro salad with chanterelles, fennel, apples and parmesan: farro simmered until tender with a bit of bite, topped with shaved apple and fennel, sauteed chanterelles and parmesan shavings in an apple vinegar vinaigrette; serves 4 as a starter or light lunch.
glance: 1 cup whole or semi-pearled, about 45 minutes (faster if semi-pearled)
2 tablespoons apple vinegar (or cider vinegar and sugar) with 1/4 cup olive oil
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the parmesan; not gluten-free
faq: How is this different from the author's first chanterelle and farro dish?

The first was a hot entree with sauteed apples and an emulsified butter sauce made with apple "balsamic" vinegar. This salad uses shaved apples, fennel and parmesan, with the same vinegar in a vinaigrette; it could lead off a dinner or be a light lunch.
How do I cook the farro?

Rinse and boil according to the package directions. If none, simmer covered in 2.5 cups of water with 1 teaspoon of salt about 45 minutes until tender. Semi-pearled farro may cook much faster. Don't let it get mushy; cool to room temperature.
What is the approach to whole grains?

They work best when you don't just use them as a substitute for refined starches: they have a nuttier, heartier, chewier character that can make them stars rather than apologetic replacements. These dishes would be unappealing with white rice.
How do I keep the apple from browning?
Shave it on a mandoline or slice it as thin as possible and toss it immediately with the lemon juice.
What can I use instead of Acetoria apple vinegar?
2 tablespoons of apple cider vinegar plus 2 teaspoons of sugar.

summary: Aromatic tofu en papillote: tofu slabs scored in both directions, sauced with soy, mirin and ginger and sealed in parchment or banana leaf packets with lemongrass, jalapeno, scallion and bell pepper, baked about 20 minutes at 400°F; serves 4 in 40 minutes.
glance: 400°F for about 20 minutes (parchment turns quite brown, which is normal)
20 ounces firm or extra-firm, 8 slabs about 1/2 inch thick
faq: Why score the tofu instead of marinating it?

Scoring it in two directions, about 1/4 inch apart and not cutting all the way through, opens up lots of surface area for the seasoning to penetrate quickly, and creates an interesting look similar to some fish preparations.
What is en papillote?
Cooking food sealed in a packet of parchment paper or banana leaves, which gives a rush of aromatic steam full of lemongrass and ginger when you open it at the table.
How do I seal the packets?

Fold the wrapper over in one direction and then the other, rolling the lip for a firm seal that's moderately tight around the ingredients but leaves a bit of room for steam, and secure with two toothpicks.
Can I customize for kids?
Yes: individual packets let you customize the spice level. For children, leave out the jalapeno and long pepper and add their favorite vegetables.
How do I serve it?
Place each packet on an individual plate, tell diners to open it carefully and enjoy the aromatic steam, and pass the lime wedges.

summary: Fried artichokes with orange-olive oil emulsion: aggressively trimmed, quartered artichokes deep-fried at 355°F (or shallow-fried) until well browned and salted, served with a dressing of simmered whole orange, sherry vinegar, Dijon and olive oil blended into an emulsion; serves 4 as an appetizer.
glance: 4 medium globe or 8 baby, quartered with the choke removed
deep fry at 355°F (preferred) or shallow fry in 1/8 inch of oil, until really well browned
1/2 orange simmered about 45 minutes, blended with vinegar, mustard and 1 cup olive oil
faq: Can I use canned artichoke hearts?
Don't even think about it: it will be terrible. Use fresh globe or baby artichokes.
How do I trim artichokes for frying?

Rub each cut surface with lemon as you work. Remove the coarse outer leaves, cut off the top third to half of the leaves, trim the stem, peel the base and stem, cut vertically into quarters and remove the choke and any pointy leaves. Be quite aggressive so everything served is fully edible.
Deep fry or shallow fry?

Deep-frying is preferable: they cook more quickly and evenly, at 355°F in enough oil to cover. Shallow frying in 1/8 inch of oil is a functional choice that wastes less oil, which is why the artichokes are quartered.
How do I make the orange-olive oil emulsion?

Simmer orange slices (skin on) in water until just a few tablespoons of liquid are left, about 45 minutes, blend with sherry vinegar, Dijon and salt, then with the blender running drizzle in the olive oil. Blend again just before serving to re-emulsify.
What inspired the emulsion?
A technique in Ottolenghi and Tamimi's Jerusalem of simmering an unpeeled orange and blitzing it into a sauce. It makes a delicious dressing, and the recipe makes more than needed for the artichokes.

summary: Harissa potatoes with feta and dill, an improvised Middle Eastern take on home fries: diced waxy potatoes browned and steamed in a covered skillet with onion, harissa, preserved lemon and cumin, then topped with feta, sumac and lots of fresh dill; about 15 minutes.
glance: 2-3 as a side dish or part of a meze
1 to 2 teaspoons harissa (less if you don't order 4 stars at the Thai place)
Vegetarian, gluten-free; vegan if you omit the feta (check the harissa and preserved lemon labels)
yield: 2-3 as a side dish or part of a meze
faq: How do I serve harissa potatoes?

As part of a meze, warm or at room temperature, with good pita, hummus, tabbouleh, a tomato salad and chickpea fritters. For a more substantial breakfast, a fried egg between the potatoes and the feta would be amazing.
How do I get the potatoes browned and tender?

Cook them with the onion and spices, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned outside and tender inside. It helps to cover the pan so the tops steam while the bottoms brown, uncovering for the last couple of minutes. You can also par-cook them in the microwave or in boiling salted water for more even, faster cooking.
How hot is it?
Harissa is a Moroccan spice paste that is quite hot; don't use the full 2 teaspoons if you don't order 4 stars at your local Thai place.
What else can I do with harissa and preserved lemon?
They keep a long time. The author lists quick mango pickle (amba), sabich and zucchini and chickpea tagine, and also spreads harissa on delivery pizza.
What potatoes should I use?
Waxy potatoes, 1/2-inch dice, skins on; Yukon Golds would be a nice choice.

summary: Tomato confit and roasted garlic bruschetta: chopped tomato confit mixed with roasted garlic (about 45 minutes at 300°F) and fresh mint, spooned on thick rustic bread brushed with olive oil and grilled; serves 4, 10 minutes if you already have confit and garlic.
glance: 10 minutes with confit and garlic already made
8 tomato confit halves, 1 head roasted garlic, 1 tablespoon sliced mint
4 thick slices rustic bread, grilled with olive oil
faq: What's the difference between crostini and bruschetta?
A crostini is generally a hard, crispy toast, while bruschetta is rustic bread brushed with olive oil and grilled.
How do I roast the garlic?

Cut off the top 1/4 inch of the head, rub with olive oil, wrap in foil and roast about 45 minutes at 300°F until completely soft and it squeezes right out of the skin. The author throws a couple of heads in during the first part of roasting tomato confit.
Can I change the herbs?
The mint adds an unexpected twist, but you can switch to oregano, basil or parsley, and add a few chopped black olives.
How do I grill the bread?
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high (a toaster oven as a last resort), brush the bread generously on one side with extra-virgin olive oil and toast until well browned with nice grill marks.
Is bruschetta vegan?
Yes, as written.

summary: Pan-seared pressed tofu with apples and champagne vinaigrette: 9 ounces of firm pressed tofu browned quickly in hot oil, tossed with a thyme-shallot champagne vinaigrette, crisp apple slices and pomegranate seeds, a hearty salad that serves 2 as a light lunch.
glance: 2 as a light lunch or 4 as a side dish
9 ounces pressed tofu, browned on both sides over high heat
champagne vinegar, shallot, thyme and olive oil, rested 10 minutes
Braeburns, 16 slices each, with 1/2 cup pomegranate seeds
yield: 2 as a light lunch or 4 as a side dish
faq: What is pressed tofu?

Tofu with so much moisture removed that it is completely firm and generally already brown with soy sauce on the outside. It browns really quickly and easily and reminds the author of grilled halloumi, which would also be excellent in this dish.
Can I use supermarket pressed tofu?

The author isn't sure you'll get the same results with the prepackaged kind, which he often finds are not just pressed but unpleasantly tough. He suggests exploring a local tofu shop; this tofu came from Northwest Tofu.
How do I make the champagne vinaigrette?

Stir together 2 tablespoons champagne vinegar, minced shallot, thyme leaves and salt, let stand 10 minutes, then drizzle in 1/4 cup of olive oil while whisking to emulsify. It's also delightful on lettuce.
Is this a salad or a main?
The apples aren't cooked and it has a vinaigrette, so it's a salad, but it's hearty enough to be a one-dish meal.
How do I cook the tofu?

Heat the oil over high heat in a large skillet, add the tofu squares in a single layer, cook until well browned on one side, flip and brown the other, then toss with the dressing before adding apples and pomegranate.

summary: Kale fried rice for one: leftover refrigerated rice crisped in a cast iron skillet about 3 minutes with garlic, cooked about 5 more minutes with sliced kale and soy sauce, then topped with a fried egg cooked in the residual heat; infinitely adaptable.
glance: 1 1/2 cups cooked and refrigerated at least a few hours
about 3 minutes for browned bits, then about 5 minutes with the kale
Vegetarian and kosher; vegan if you omit the egg; gluten-free with gluten-free soy sauce
faq: Why does fried rice need leftover rice?
It only works with leftover rice that has sat in the fridge for at least a few hours.
How do I make it vegan, spicier or with more protein?

Skip the egg for vegan; add small cubes of tofu or tempeh for protein; for spice use any fresh or dried chili pepper, curry spices, a Chinese chili paste, sriracha or harissa. Just pick one general culinary tradition and stick with it.
Can I use another green?
Yes: spinach, cabbage or any leafy green, or other vegetables as long as you allow for the time they need to cook.
Can I use brown or black rice?
Yes. Brown rice, red rice or black rice work as well.
How do I make it for a group?
You'll need a bigger skillet or wok so there's plenty of surface area to crisp up the rice.
How is it different from traditional fried rice?
The egg isn't scrambled in. The rice is toasted in a bit of oil for crispy, brown bits, then a fried egg goes on top, cooked with the skillet's residual heat.

summary: Grilled pizza with fingerling potatoes, blue cheese and caramelized onions: thin 12-inch rounds of 00-flour dough grilled about a minute directly on very hot embers, flipped, topped and closed under the lid about another minute; makes two pizzas.
glance: two 200-gram balls, stretched nearly transparent in the middle
about 1 minute on the first side, flip, top, close the lid about 1 more minute
faq: What is the grilled pizza technique?

Skip the pizza stone and cook directly on a very hot grate: grill the naked dough on one side until starting to char, flip, and immediately apply toppings, then close the lid about a minute. That avoids a cooked bottom but doughy edges.
What flour should I use?
The author recommends 00 (double-zero) flour and following his perfected dough recipe to the letter, ideally by weight, paying attention to the times and rests so the dough hydrates properly.
How thin should the dough be?
Stretch each ball into a roughly 12-inch circle, nearly transparent in the middle and maybe 1/4 inch thick at the edges, ideally in the air, letting gravity work.
Why preheat the toppings?
If they are cold they won't have enough time to get hot, so use warm or at least room-temperature toppings, and have everything prepared within reach of the grill.
What tools do I need?
A pizza peel is best; if the grate is below the grill's edge, a very large offset spatula helps. Be very careful: the author says don't do anything you aren't comfortable doing safely.
What grill does the author use?
A Big Green Egg, which gets to crazy high temperatures. You'll need to experiment with your own setup: preheat very high but let the flames die down so you have very hot embers.
